fills.researcher_notes: UNRESOLVED for a specific commissioning year, despite finding strong context. The brief pointed at SNGPL's 'province-wise transmission breakdown' document as the lead the sweep used to confirm existence -- I located and read that exact document (SNGPL website article 'Province-Wise Transmission Breakup', pgids=461/artids=341) and it gives only current AGGREGATE km totals per province (Baluchistan/Sindh/KPK/Punjab), no per-segment names or dates, so it cannot answer Date_logic for any individual line; noted so nobody re-chases it for a date. What DOES exist, from a different SNGPL document family: (1) SNGPL's own 'History of SNGPL' page (sngpl.com.pk/web/page.jsp?pgids=322) and the Wikipedia mirror of the same text (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sui_Northern_Gas_Pipelines_Limited) both state SNGPL, on its 1963 incorporation (public company Jan 1964), 'took over the existing Sui-Multan System (217 miles of 16 inch and 80 miles of 10 inch diameter pipelines) from Pakistan Industrial Development Corporation (PIDC)' -- i.e. a Sui-Multan gas system already existed and was already called 'existing' before SNGPL's own founding, so it predates 1963/64. (2) SNGPL's Annual Report 2017 'MILESTONES' company timeline (printed p.52-53; large PDF, verifier false-negative, manually confirmed) lists 'PROJECT I: Extension of Sui-Multan section to Faisalabad and Lahore and then linked with Dhulian-Rawalpindi-Wah system to form a common grid' against the bracket '1964-1969' -- an EXTENSION, not the original build, again implying an earlier base date. Neither source, nor any further search, names the specific year the ORIGINAL Sui-Multan line (16in+10in, per PIDC) went into service, and the CURRENT row's spec (24in, 288.06 km) does not match those original PIDC diameters at all -- it is confirmed as today's exact asset by SNGPL's FY2018 asset register ('TRANSMISSION SYSTEM As at June 30, 2018', SNGPLAR-2018.pdf printed p.33, row 27: 'SUI-MULTAN / 24 / 288.06' km mainline, an EXACT match), which strongly suggests the modern 24in/288km line is a later rebuild/uprate of the 1960s system rather than the literal original pipe, and no source dates that rebuild either. Recommend treating StartYear1 as genuinely unresolvable to a single year from available sources rather than guessing a value inside the pre-1964 window; a human may choose to record something like 'pre-1964 (predates SNGPL's own founding; original PIDC construction date not found)' as a documented caveat instead of a bare year.
fills.not_a_fill_caveat: values/primary_value/proposed_refs deliberately empty -- see researcher_notes for the full documented dead end.

validity.recommendation: No action needed on existence or current spec (already confirmed by Leg 1/2 and independently re-confirmed here). Consider adding a ResearcherNotes caveat that the modern 24in/288.06km asset is very likely a rebuild of the pre-1964 PIDC-era Sui-Multan system rather than that original pipe, so a future researcher doesn't try to force a 1960s date onto today's diameter/length.
validity.researcher_notes: SNGPL's FY2018 transmission asset register (SNGPLAR-2018.pdf, printed p.33, row 27) lists 'SUI-MULTAN / 24 / 288.06' km mainline -- an exact match to this row's current Diameter and LengthKnown, confirming the row describes SNGPL's real, currently-in-service asset. The ORIGINAL Sui-Multan system taken over from PIDC at SNGPL's 1963/64 founding was 217 miles of 16in + 80 miles of 10in pipe (per SNGPL's own History page and the Wikipedia mirror) -- different diameters entirely from today's 24in line, and SNGPL's 2017 Annual Report milestone timeline records a 1964-1969 'extension' project on top of that. The clean inference is that today's 24in/288km line is a later reconstruction/uprate of the historic corridor, not the 1960s pipe itself -- consistent with the corridor being 'one of the oldest and most-cited pipelines in Pakistan' while carrying a spec that postdates the 1960s hardware.
